question: Does each account get its own genuine canvas/WebGL/audio rendering, not shared with our other accounts?
Does the device tell no lies a consistency checker (CreepJS, FP-Scanner, Meta) can catch, e.g. GPU name vs pixels, OS vs fonts, engine vs user agent?
Does the account present the same device every session, for months?
Does it look like an ordinary person's home device rather than a datacenter, VM, emulator or automation fleet?
Does everything (IP, timezone, locale, latency, DNS, WebRTC) consistently say the account's country with no trace of Vietnam?
If one account is banned or checkpointed, how well are the others protected from being linked to it (device, cookies, IP, host)?
How strong is the independent evidence (live tests, issues, papers) that this option actually works, rather than vendor claims?
How well does it reuse what log-cli already has (Camoufox gate, launch self-check, pinned device in Twenty, local hours, proxy handling)?
How cheap is it per account per month at 10 accounts?
How little engineering time to get the first account running on it?
How little day-to-day work does it need (maintenance, babysitting, hardware, updates)?
How easily does it grow from 3 to 50 accounts without new linkage or cost cliffs?
How well do we keep control of the accounts' cookies, credentials and sessions (not held by a third party)?
How easy is it to back out or switch away later (no lock-in)?
How well does it match how real Marketplace sellers use Facebook (mobile app vs desktop web, posting photos, messaging buyers)?
How well does it handle Facebook/Arkose captchas and checkpoints with the account's own IP and device (in-browser solving, no foreign solver IP)?
